_doc: The farmsteads' families (the user's list of 2026-11-08b, docs/improvements9.txt: 'farm families to go with the farms'): what each says when she speaks to them (F), by who they are; 'any' is said by every one. {farm} is the farmstead's name. 899 farms writes them into brokenspire's generator (WildFarmLines, '<who>|<line>'), and the paddock's most animals (WildFarmAnimalsMax).

farmer: The strips by the lane are mine this year, barley. The headland's for turning the plough, mind your step.
Ridge and furrow, same as my father ploughed it. The water runs off into the furrows and the crop stays dry.
One crop to the whole field, that's the rule. The reeve says wheat, it's wheat, from this hedge to the far one.
Wolves took two of the neighbour's sheep last moon. Keep to the road after dark.
If you're bound for Brokenspire, tell the miller I'll bring the grain once the rain stops.
farmwife: Mind the gate, they'll be out and in the beans before you can whistle.
Hens are laying again. That's the first good news since the frost.
We keep the little plots by the house for ourselves: cabbages, peas, a few beans. The open field's for the lord's tithe as much as ours.
You look half starved. There's bread in the house if you've a coin for it.
Welcome to {farm}. Don't mind the mud.
farmhand: Up before the cock, down after the sun. Pay's a roof and two meals.
Barn's full of hay to the rafters. Somebody's going to have to fork it all again come spring.
I'd rather be swinging a sword like you than a scythe, truth be told.
The old boundary stones? They say the strips haven't moved in a hundred years.
child: Are you a knight? Did you kill a dragon?
I'm minding the well. Nobody's allowed to fall in.
Ma says not to talk to strangers. But you're not strange, you're just dusty.
any: The harvest won't bring itself in.
